charter: Explore the CSV receipt import with malformed, oversized, and wrong-encoding files (and files from another tenant's export) to discover how the parser fails, whether it corrupts existing receipts, and whether any row can leak across tenants.

areas_covered: Parser on valid, truncated, 250 MB, UTF-16, embedded-comma and <tenant B>-exported files
Post-import receipt list and running expense total
Import error banner and per-row rejection report

notes.text: Baseline: a clean 40-row CSV imports cleanly and the total updates; kept as the did-I-break-something oracle.
A file cut mid-row imports 39 rows and silently drops the partial 40th; is that intended?
The import screen restricts no file type; a renamed .exe is accepted for upload.
A CSV exported from <tenant B> imported into <tenant A> with no tenant check at all.

bugs.summary: CSV import does not scope rows to the current tenant
bugs.repro: Log in as <tenant A>; open the CSV import screen; import a receipts CSV exported from <tenant B>'s account.
bugs.observed: All 40 rows were accepted and attributed to <tenant A>; they appear in <tenant A>'s receipt list and running total.
bugs.why_wrong: Data must never cross tenants; the import accepted another tenant's export without any ownership check.
bugs.oracle: Never/Always invariant: data never crosses tenants
bugs.minimal_repro: Import any CSV exported from <tenant B> while logged in as <tenant A>; one row is enough.
bugs.worst_observed: <tenant B>'s receipt rows, vendor names and amounts persisted under <tenant A>.
bugs.generalization: Reproduced with a 1-row and a 40-row export; not tried with other tenant pairs.
bugs.stakeholder_impact: Every tenant: another tenant's expense data can be imported into, and read from, the wrong account.

bugs.summary: UTF-16 CSVs import accented vendor names as mojibake, silently
bugs.repro: As <tenant A>, import a UTF-16-encoded CSV whose vendor column contains "Café Subroute".
bugs.observed: The receipt list shows "CafÃ© Subroute"; no warning or rejection was shown.
bugs.why_wrong: The help text claims UTF-8 support; the accepted data is now stored wrong and exports wrong.
bugs.oracle: Consistency with claims (the import help text)
bugs.minimal_repro: A one-row UTF-16 CSV with one accented vendor name.
bugs.worst_observed: The corrupted vendor name persisted and appeared the same way in a subsequent export.
bugs.generalization: Also fails for a UTF-16 file with a byte-order mark; UTF-8 files with the same names import correctly.
bugs.stakeholder_impact: Finance users importing from tools that export UTF-16: vendor names are silently corrupted and must be fixed by hand.

bugs.summary: A 250 MB upload fails with a generic error that names no limit or row
bugs.repro: As <tenant A>, upload a 250 MB synthetic receipts CSV on the import screen.
bugs.observed: The request eventually failed with "Something went wrong" and no file-size limit or row detail.
bugs.why_wrong: An error the user cannot act on: it names neither the limit nor what to change.
bugs.minimal_repro: not established: only the one 250 MB file was tried; the threshold size is unknown
bugs.worst_observed: The upload failed with a generic error; whether any rows persisted was not checked.
bugs.generalization: not established: size probes were capped after this one cost 9 of 34 tool calls
bugs.stakeholder_impact: Provisional: does a failed oversized upload persist any rows? Users with large exports cannot tell what to change.
bugs.replicated: not established: the one oversized upload cost 9 of 34 tool calls and was not re-run

questions_risks.text: Is silently dropping a truncated final row acceptable, or should the import fail loudly?
Does a failed oversized upload persist any rows? (decides the 250 MB bug's magnitude)
No server-side file-type validation was observed; only the absent client check.

off_charter.item: No file-type restriction on the import upload; a renamed .exe is accepted.
off_charter.candidate_charter: Explore the import upload with disallowed and disguised file types to discover missing server-side validation.

off_charter.item: A rapid double-submit of the same import was not tested for double counting.
off_charter.candidate_charter: Explore the import submit with rapid repeated submissions to discover whether receipts or totals are double-counted.

known_bad.summary: Receipt dates display in UTC rather than the tenant's time zone
known_bad.observed: Imported receipts dated 23:30 local time show the next day's date in the list.
known_bad.basis: known_issues: EF-112 receipt dates display in UTC

debrief.explored: Charter #1 on the CSV import as <tenant A>: valid, truncated, 250 MB, UTF-16, embedded-comma and cross-tenant files, with Follow the Data, Violate Format, Goldilocks and Change the Model. 7 of 12 probes; stopped because the charter went quiet.
debrief.found: A Critical cross-tenant import (3/3), a High UTF-16 mojibake (2/2), a provisional Moderate generic error on a 250 MB upload, and one known-bad UTC date display (EF-112) noted, not re-reported.
debrief.unknown: Whether a failed oversized upload persists rows; the intended file-size limit; whether a truncated final row may be dropped silently.

proof.past: One budgeted session against charter #1 on the demo target.
proof.results: 3 bugs (Critical 1, High 1, Moderate 1), 3 questions or risks, 2 off-charter items, 1 known-bad.
proof.obstacles: Oversized-file probes were setup-heavy; size probes were capped after one.
proof.outlook: Charter the upload file-type and double-submit items; re-check the cross-tenant fix in a follow-up session.
proof.feelings: Uneasy about tenant isolation beyond import; the cross-tenant bug suggests other import paths may skip the check.
